reason: The hypothesis merges two distinct interventions from different alloy systems: L12 precipitation strengthening (E4, E5 on Al0.7CoCrFeNi) and a duplex microstructure with hierarchical constraint effects (E2, E3 on AlCoCrFeNi2.1). No cited evidence demonstrates the combined effect on the specified starting state, and the application boundaries (creep, corrosion, temperature fluctuations) are entirely unsupported. The premises are thus only partly supported, with a major gap in evidence for the merged intervention.
premises: Low-temperature annealing precipitates ordered L12 intermetallics in the FCC phase of AlCoCrFeNi-based EHEAs, strengthening via Orowan mechanism
Thermo-mechanical processing can create an ultrafine-grained duplex microstructure in AlCoCrFeNi2.1 EHEA
The ultrafine-grained duplex microstructure improves strength-ductility synergy via a two-hierarchical constraint effect and microcrack-arresting mechanism
The combined intervention (annealing + thermo-mechanical processing) will enhance strength and ductility for the target application conditions
The proposed mechanisms and outcomes apply to the uniform, fine lamellar starting state of AlCoCrFeNi2.1
